faqs.question: Which model should I start with for a general-purpose assistant?
faqs.answer: Granite 4.2 8B is the recommended starting point for most production workloads. It offers a strong balance of quality across coding, RAG, instruction following, and multilingual support without the compute cost of the 30B model. Move to 3B if you need lower latency or on-device deployment, or to 30B if you need maximum reasoning quality.

faqs.question: What's the difference between Granite Vision and Granite Docling?
faqs.answer:
Both are Granite vision-language models (VLMs), but they're built for different jobs in a document pipeline. 

Granite Vision 4.1 4B is a 4B-parameter model purpose-built for structured document extraction. Think pulling targeted data out of document images, such as converting charts to CSV/code, extracting complex tables to JSON/HTML, and performing schema-based key-value pair extraction (e.g., pulling an invoice date or order number), delivering near-frontier accuracy at a fraction of the size of larger general VLMs. 

Granite Docling 258M, by contrast, is a much smaller (258M-parameter) model purpose-built for full-page document conversion — reading an entire page's layout (text, tables, code, formulas, charts) and reproducing it faithfully as a structured, machine-readable document (Markdown, HTML, or DocTags) via the open-source Docling toolkit, rather than pulling out isolated fields. 

In short: Granite Vision answers targeted questions about specific elements within a document, while Granite Docling reconstructs the whole document's structure end-to-end — and the two can be combined, with Granite Vision plugging into Docling pipelines to add deeper visual understanding to specific extraction steps.

faqs.question: How do the Embedding models differ from the Language models for RAG?
faqs.answer:
Embedding models and Language models solve different problems in a RAG pipeline. An Embedding model converts text into dense numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning, so that a query and a relevant passage end up close together in vector space even if they don't share the same words — this is what makes fast, meaning-based retrieval over large document collections possible. A Language model, by contrast, doesn't retrieve anything; it generates fluent text, reasoning over whatever context it's given to produce an answer. 

In a typical RAG pipeline, the two work in sequence: an Embedding model retrieves the most relevant passages for a query, an optional Reranker re-scores those passages for precision, and a Language model then generates the final answer grounded in that retrieved context. Using the right model for each step — rather than asking a Language model to also handle retrieval — keeps the pipeline both faster and more accurate at scale.

faqs.question: What are GraniteLib adapters and when should I use them?
faqs.answer: GraniteLib models are LoRA adapters — small, modular extensions that attach to a Granite base model to add or enhance specific capabilities (RAG, safety, general instruction-following) without full fine-tuning. Use them when you want to customize a base model cheaply and composably, rather than deploying a separate specialized model.

faqs.question: What is Granite Switch, and when should I use it instead of separate Language, Guardian, and Speech models?
faqs.answer:
Granite Switch is a modular LLM: a single checkpoint that combines a Granite 4.1 base model with embedded LoRA adapters and a speech encoder. Granite Switch 4.1 8B and 30B ship with the guardian-core adapter for safety checks, the decision adapter for scoring a question against labelled options, and Granite Speech TurboCTC for English speech-to-text. You pick an adapter per request through the chat template (adapter_name), so one running server handles chat, safety checks, decisions, and transcription. 

Choose Switch when you need several of those capabilities together and want one endpoint and one GPU footprint — the 8B needs roughly half the VRAM of running Granite 4.1 8B, Guardian 4.1 8B, and a speech model side by side. Choose the separate models when you only need one capability, need multilingual speech (Switch's speech path is English-only), or need Guardian's full set of risk checks rather than guardian-core. You can also compose your own Switch checkpoint from the Granite Libraries adapters with the open-source granite-switch composer.

faqs.question: Can I combine multiple Granite models in a pipeline?
faqs.answer: Yes — this is a common pattern. For example: Granite Embedding for retrieval, Granite Reranker for precision, Granite Language for generation, Granite Guardian for safety checking. Each model is optimized for its step in the pipeline.
